key_insight: The paper extends a previously discovered mathematical equivalence between two-dimensional vortical free-boundary flows without surface tension and irrotational capillary flows to a new pair of problems: a hollow vortex in shear/strain and a surface-tension bubble in a straining flow.
engineering_relevance: This analogy lets researchers transfer analytical and numerical techniques between seemingly different fluid-structure problems, potentially simplifying the design and prediction of free-surface and vortex-dominated flows.
method: Constructs an exact isolated solution for the special case γ = 0.
Computes numerical solutions for nonzero γ.
Shows that conformal-mapping identities from capillary flows also apply to hollow vortex problems under parameter constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both an exact analytical solution at γ = 0 and numerical solutions for nonzero γ, supporting the proposed extension of the analogy.
watch_item: The correspondence may require special parameter constraints and may not hold directly for all flow configurations or perturbations.
paper_title: Extension of a mathematical analogy between vortical flows without surface tension and irrotational capillary flows
